answer: Grader-panel diversity resists sybil rings: a verdict is final only when its panel spans provably distinct trust neighborhoods, so no single kin-cluster can supply a quorum. A ring is one island of mutually-linked fakes; it cannot populate a diverse panel because its members all share one neighborhood, like a crew from a single pearl-boat crewing their own voyage. Requiring graders from separated regions of the trust graph means a collusive cluster can never assemble enough independent seats to pass its own work.
